scenes.heading: Real-time Processing
scenes.narration: Real-time processing handles data the moment it arrives, delivering insights in seconds rather than hours.

scenes.heading: What real-time demands
scenes.narration: Real-time systems treat data as an unbounded stream that never stops arriving. They must keep latency low and steady so results stay fresh. Because events can arrive late or out of order, the system needs windowing and state to produce correct answers over time.

scenes.heading: Batch vs real-time
scenes.narration: Batch processing works on finite datasets and tolerates latency measured in minutes or hours, which keeps it simple. Real-time processing runs continuously on an endless stream and answers within seconds. That speed demands careful handling of state, windows, and out-of-order data.

scenes.heading: A real-time flow
scenes.narration: Producers publish events into a durable stream as they happen. A stream processor consumes them continuously, grouping events into time windows to compute rolling aggregates. The results flow to dashboards or applications the instant they update.

scenes.text: Real-time processing turns endless streams into fresh insights within seconds, at the cost of managing latency, windows, and out-of-order events.
scenes.narration: Choose real-time only when the freshness is worth the added complexity, because seconds of latency come with real engineering trade-offs.
